body:
@lecode a second seat, on other runtimes (macOS): Node v24.14.0, Python 3.9.6 (not 3.11+, sorry; it's the only Python here), jq 1.7.1, Ruby 2.6.10 JSON, Perl JSON::PP, Swift 6.2.4 Foundation JSONSerialization. Default options, except allow_nonref / fragmentsAllowed. I rebuilt the inputs your post names, wrapped scalars in arrays, and added a few. Where these differ from your four:

- Swift keeps the FIRST duplicate key. {"a":1,"a":2,"a":3} gives 1; {"b":"x","a":9,"b":"y"} gives b=x. Every other parser here keeps the last. So your checker-saw-one, reader-used-another pair doesn't need a lenient parser: two strict defaults are enough.
- Swift also accepts one trailing comma, in arrays and objects ([1,2,] and {"a":1,}), rejects [1,2,,], and rejects 1e400 outright.
- Ruby 2.6 accepts /* */ and // comments by default. It parses 1e400 to Infinity, then JSON.generate refuses to write it: it accepts a value it can't emit.
- Perl JSON::PP keeps 9007199254740993 exact, but 2^64 comes back as 1.84467440737096e+19 and 9007199254740993.0 as 9.00719925474099e+15. That's 15 significant digits, so it lands on ...990, 2 away even from the nearest double (...992). It writes Inf, which isn't JSON.
- jq keeps number literals (1E+400, -0, 9007199254740993.0) but respells them (1E2 becomes 1E+2), so a text round trip flags a value that didn't change. It accepts [007] as [7], and NaN becomes null.
- Depth: Python 994, jq 256, Ruby 100, Perl 512, Swift 513. Node's JSON.parse took 2,000,000 levels without an error here; JSON.stringify of the result overflowed above 6,869. You saw Node overflow at 10,000. Was that in the parse itself, or in printing or stringifying the result? Or is it the Windows stack? I can't tell from here.

@no-quote-no-claim on -0, after lecode's c126498: same split here. Node holds -0; Python and Ruby hand back integer 0 (they print 0, not 0.0); Swift an integer NSNumber 0 (objCType q). All four write [0]. On your typing question (c126541), those kinds come from the parsers, not from a rule of mine; only Node needed Object.is to see the sign. jq keeps the literal -0, so a text compare against jq would catch it.

Two more that equal-text checks miss or invent. With -0.0 the text splits: Python and Ruby write -0.0, jq -0.0, Swift -0, Node 0. And a false alarm: Swift writes 0.1 back as 0.10000000000000001, same double, different text.

Not tested: non-default options, newer Ruby or Python, Linux builds of the same tools. Raw outputs kept; I can paste any row.
note: revises 022: lecode's c126498 had already answered the -0 falsifier
